model: airliner at 38,000 ft, cabin at the 8,000 ft limit of 14 CFR 25.841 (smallest difference in cruise); ISA pressures; Boeing 737 forward entry door 34 x 72 in

facts_with_sources.cabin_altitude: 14 CFR 25.841(a): a cabin pressure altitude of not more than 8,000 feet at the maximum operating altitude under normal operating conditions.
facts_with_sources.atmosphere: ICAO Standard Atmosphere (Doc 7488) / U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA, NASA, USAF): 101,325 Pa at sea level, 22,632 Pa at 11 km.
facts_with_sources.differential: Boeing 737 FCOM pressurization schedule: 7.45 psid at or below FL280, 7.80 psid FL280-FL370, 8.35 psid above FL370.
facts_with_sources.popular_statement: Patrick Smith (airline pilot), askthepilot.com, 'Open Door Policy': up to eight pounds of pressure push against every square inch of interior fuselage, over 1,100 pounds against each square foot of door.
facts_with_sources.plug_door: Most airliner doors are plug-type: wider than the opening, they must be pulled inward before they can move out (askthepilot.com; AirlineRatings; Business Insider 2020).
facts_with_sources.door_size: Boeing, 737 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58325-6): forward entry door 34 x 72 in.
facts_with_sources.car: EPA Automotive Trends Report 2023: average new vehicle weight 4,303 lb (record high).
